question.text: Assume that protons and neutrons have equal masses. Mass of a nucleon is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and radius of nucleus is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The approximate ratio of the nuclear density and water density is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>13</mn></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> is _____.

solution.text:
As we know, density of nuclei= mass of nuclei  volume of nuclei 

⇒ρ=1.6×10-27A43π1.5×10-153A

=1.6×10-2714.14×10-45=0.113×1018 kg m-3

We also know that, density of water is ρw=103 kg m-3.

Hence,
ρρw=11.31×1013.

Therefore, n≈11
